title: Access policy for Browser Access: client type and unsupported criteria

prose.text: Browser Access sessions are matched by client type in access policy, and the Web Browser client type limits which other criteria a rule may use.

prose.label: Targeting.

checks.do: Which client type value the rule or Terraform resource uses for browser sessions, and that the provider documents the exporter value for it.
Whether a rule intended for browser users also carries posture, trusted network or country criteria that the help says do not apply.
Whether a posture-related deny for a browser session can be explained by a source or is the unverified outcome.

web-browser-client-type.statement: An access policy rule can target the Web Browser client type, which refers to Browser Access. Multiple client types in one rule are joined with OR.

quotes: Web Browser: To learn more, see About Browser Access.
If you added multiple client types to the policy rule, Private Access uses an OR Boolean operator between them.

web-browser-client-type.conditions: Statement changed: the list of other client types was removed because it is not in the quotes.

exporter-operand.statement: In the Terraform provider's Browser Access policy rule documentation, the CLIENT_TYPE operand value zpn_client_type_exporter is the one that enforces access via browser access to application segments, and zpn_client_type_zappl is the one for Client Connector.

quotes: zpn_client_type_exporter` - Used to support/enforce access via browser access tp application segments.
zpn_client_type_zappl` - Used to support/enforce access via Zscaler Client Connector to application segments.

browser-isolation-client-type.statement: The Go SDK client-type list defines zpn_client_type_browser_isolation as a separate client type from zpn_client_type_exporter and zpn_client_type_zapp.

no-posture-with-web-browser.statement: Rules that use the Web Browser or Internet & SaaS Service Edge client types cannot also use posture profiles or trusted networks criteria, which only work with Client Connector.

quotes: Rules using the Web Browser or Internet & SaaS Service Edge client types additionally can't use posture profiles or trusted networks criteria. The posture profiles or trusted networks criteria only work with Client Connector.

country-codes-unsupported.statement: The Country Codes criteria type is not supported in Browser Access or Privileged Remote Access applications.

quotes: The Country Codes criteria type is not supported in Browser Access or Privileged Remote Access Applications.

posture-rule-outcome.title: What a Browser Access session gets from a rule that has a posture condition
posture-rule-outcome.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "A policy rule with a posture condition (POSTURE operand) will never match for Browser Access sessions - the posture result is absent, which is treated as failure. The user gets a generic deny response with no explanation that posture is the cause." The help says a rule using the Web Browser client type cannot also use posture profiles (claim no-posture-with-web-browser). It does not describe how a rule that mixes a posture condition with other client types evaluates for a browser session, or what the user sees. A lab test with a mixed rule and a browser session would resolve it.

browser-isolation-operand.title: What zpn_client_type_browser_isolation matches
browser-isolation-operand.detail: The legacy reference named zpn_client_type_browser_isolation as the Browser Access client type. The provider documentation names zpn_client_type_exporter for that role (claim exporter-operand), and the Go SDK lists the browser-isolation value separately (claim browser-isolation-client-type). Which sessions the browser-isolation value matches, and whether it applies to Browser Access at all, is not stated. A lab test that sets each operand and observes a Browser Access session would resolve it.
